tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Star Properties & Classification

questions.question: Q: What is the difference between apparent and absolute magnitude?
questions.correctAnswer: Apparent magnitude is how bright a star looks from Earth. Absolute magnitude is the brightness it would have if placed at a standard distance of 10 parsecs.

questions.question: Q: State the spectral classes from hottest to coolest.
questions.correctAnswer: O, B, A, F, G, K, M (mnemonic: Oh Be A Fine Girl/Guy, Kiss Me).

questions.question: Q: How is stellar parallax used to measure distance?
questions.correctAnswer: A star's apparent shift against background stars is measured over 6 months. Distance in parsecs = 1/parallax angle in arcseconds.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Star Properties & Classification

questions.question: Q: Why do blue stars appear brighter than red stars of the same size?
questions.correctAnswer: Blue stars are hotter, and luminosity depends on temperature (L ∝ T⁴), so hotter stars emit far more energy per unit area.

questions.question: Q: What is the inverse square law of light?
questions.correctAnswer: Apparent brightness decreases proportionally to 1/d², where d is the distance from the star.
